site.name: GTA VI PC Tracker
site.description: Live standings of the unofficial projects trying to run the Xbox build of GTA VI on a PC: how far each has got, what changed, and a best guess at when it becomes playable.

headline_note: None is playable yet. The best picture is lit only where sunlight falls, at 2 to 4 frames a second.

stages.name: Loads
stages.bar: The game's executable loads with its imports resolved.

stages.name: Starts up
stages.bar: The game's own start-up code runs: memory, threads, archives.

stages.name: Graphics device
stages.bar: The game creates its graphics device and queues on the PC.

stages.name: First frames
stages.bar: Frames are presented to a window, even if they are black.

stages.name: Recognisable picture
stages.bar: The game's own screens can be seen: logos, menus, video or setup pages.

stages.name: In-game
stages.bar: The game world is loaded and running, with or without a usable picture.

stages.name: Playable
stages.bar: 30 minutes or more in the world under player control, at 20 frames a second or better, without a crash.

projects.name: victory-gta6
projects.tagline: Fork of VIctory aimed at a correct, playable picture
projects.furthest: The first gameplay scene, lit by sunlight, with the player in control
projects.status: Plays the opening cutscene lit and in order, then renders the first gameplay scene with characters, textures, sky and a sunlit exterior; the HUD, pause menu and gamepad work. Anything out of direct sunlight is black because ray-traced light does not run yet. The world runs at 2 to 4 frames a second, or 240 to 350 ms a frame with opt-in switches. A device loss added by a wave64 update was fixed on 24 Nov, and the README now reports no hang or device loss in normal runs.
projects.source: the fork's own README section (dated 25 Nov) and commit e9765a7, tested on one RTX 4070

projects.name: AnyXboxX
projects.tagline: Xbox Series emulator focused on this one game, built on VIctory
projects.furthest: About 13 minutes in the starting area with a picture, at about 4 fps
projects.status: Since merging PR #167 it runs the world on the victory-gta6 fork, pinned at commit d279e69. Its README reports the maintainer playing about 13 minutes in the starting area at about 4 frames a second, with the 3D picture shown, the character under control and the first characters met. The host device is still lost after a few minutes to about 13; the pinned commit predates the fork's device-loss fix.
projects.source: project README after merged PR #167; observed by the maintainer on an RTX 4070 SUPER

projects.name: ScarlettPort
projects.tagline: Packages VIctory and XCL with its own fixes and launcher; started 24 Nov
projects.furthest: The movement tutorial prompt; the 3D picture behind it is black
projects.status: Its README says that on an RTX 3060, using VIctory with community pull requests, the game gets past its opening to the movement tutorial at about 1 frame a second. The final picture is black because some lighting shaders do not translate yet; a debug view shows the world's geometry. A second path on XCL runs the menus and loading screens at 30 fps.
projects.source: project README and commit 87116d5 (24 Nov), one RTX 3060; this page has not checked its prebuilt launcher

projects.name: VIctory
projects.tagline: Runs the game's Xbox code natively on Windows
projects.furthest: The first mission's title card; the world behind it stays dark
projects.status: The upstream code base that victory-gta6 and AnyXboxX build on. Its README boots the game, runs the menus at 30 fps and loads into the world in about 50 seconds, where the first mission's title card renders but the scene after it stays dark, at 0.5 to 1.8 seconds a frame. Entering the world can hang a real graphics card.
projects.source: project README (status dated 23 Nov), tested on one RX 6700 XT

projects.name: Palmwave
projects.tagline: Xbox Series to Windows layer with its own shader path
projects.furthest: The first mission, with part of its geometry drawn and the picture one flat colour (modified run)
projects.status: The first mission starts and part of the world's geometry is drawn, such as poles, power lines and fences, but about 91% of the depth buffer is empty and the picture is one flat colour because nothing is lit yet. A world frame takes about 10 seconds. The runs use an unmerged branch and ten byte patches to the game, which switch off its hang detector and several heavy render passes.
projects.source: project README; a modified run on an unmerged branch, RTX 5080

projects.name: CGBJ
projects.tagline: Private build, reportedly based on VIctory. No public code
projects.furthest: A player walking in an unlit world, according to press reports (unconfirmed)
projects.status: Press coverage has described a private build in the game world with a player walking, unlit and very slow. Nobody outside the group can test it, and this page has found no first-hand source, so it ranks last in stage 6.
projects.source: press reports only; not confirmed by this page

projects.name: five-star-recomp
projects.tagline: Native recompilation of the Xbox Series release
projects.furthest: Story mode loads as far as the story intro's title card
projects.status: Starts, shows the logo, intro art and first-run screens, loads story mode and reaches the story intro's title card, then stops. All 25,908 of the game's shader programs translate and compile.
projects.source: project README and wiki status page

projects.name: OpenScarlett (Community Edition)
projects.tagline: Xbox Series runtime for Windows and Linux
projects.furthest: The start screen after the intro movie, at 30 fps
projects.status: Runs the first-boot settings, legal and start screens at 30 fps and plays the 4K intro movie with sound, then stops while it streams in the scene behind the menus. About nine in ten of the game's shaders translate.
projects.source: project README (it calls the game "a newer retail game")

projects.name: PercyScarlett
projects.tagline: Xbox Series runtime; already runs Minecraft's Series build in-world
projects.furthest: The whole first-run setup, then the world starts to stream in
projects.status: Renders the account picker, plays the game's 4K video and walks through the full first-run setup with a gamepad, saving settings and starting to stream the world.
projects.source: project README, which refers to the game by a nickname

projects.name: XCL
projects.tagline: General Xbox Series to Windows compatibility layer, in the spirit of Proton
projects.furthest: The menus and settings screens, at 30 fps
projects.status: Starts the game in about four seconds and holds a steady 30 fps through its menus and on to the settings screens without crashing. Gameplay is not reached yet. All 26,698 of the game's GPU programs translate.
projects.source: project README (it calls the game "a newer retail game")

projects.name: Xbox2Windows
projects.tagline: Static recompiler and runtime for Xbox Series executables
projects.furthest: The intro, the setup text and a loading screen (modified build)
projects.status: A modified diagnostic build, which skips failed checks automatically, played the intro, showed readable setup text and reached loading on an RTX 4060 laptop. Starting the original executable is not yet shown.
projects.source: project README and its progress issue

projects.name: g6shim
projects.tagline: Stand-in system libraries for the Series release
projects.furthest: The account picker, at about 12 fps
projects.status: Starts the game, opens all its archives and renders its screens up to the account picker at about 12 frames a second. About 84% of the game's shaders translate. A commit on 24 Nov adds an offline console with one signed-in user, the README's next step, but no new screen is reported yet.
projects.source: project README (it names the game by its title ID, 7952987A) and commit 9f5bd4f

projects.name: TuxBox
projects.tagline: Runs Xbox Series games on Linux through Proton
projects.status: Shows the game's player-selection prompt at 3840 by 2160 on stock Proton Experimental. It is the furthest Linux-first project.

projects.name: GTA6-BootTest
projects.tagline: Boot harness with stand-in libraries and its own shader translator
projects.furthest: The prompt bar of the start screen; the screens after it are black
projects.status: Boots, streams its archives, runs the frame loop and draws its first interface screen, the start-screen prompt bar, through translated shaders. Screens after that go black again.

projects.name: OpenScarlett
projects.tagline: Xbox Series runtime; plays Minecraft's Series build at 60 fps
projects.furthest: The game's 4K interface and a full-colour video render, according to its commits
projects.status: Commit ef763eb says GTA VI finishes all 249 of its start-up tasks and runs its interface loop at 30 fps. Two later commits that day report the retail title's interface rendering at 3840 by 2160 on a GTX 1650 Ti (f8e24d4) and full-colour 4K video playback (c382f68). They do not name the title again or say which screens were reached, so it ranks last in stage 5.
projects.source: commits ef763eb, f8e24d4 and c382f68 (24 Nov); the README does not cover the game yet

projects.name: palmetto
projects.tagline: Solo clean-room runtime, started from Leonida's work
projects.furthest: A window shows presented frames, all black
projects.status: Commits on 24 Nov wire the game's present call to a real window and put the game's memory pages into the graphics card's address space, so draws now execute without a hang. A 150-second run submitted about 15,500 draws and as many presents with no device loss, but a read-back of the drawn target is uniformly black. The README still describes the older state.
projects.source: commits 523d947, ea771ec and 38c8451, measured on an RTX 4090

projects.name: xbox-emulator
projects.tagline: General Xbox Series runtime, a continuation of TomBox
projects.furthest: Six minutes of presented frames, all black (contributor's branch)
projects.status: A contributor reports running the game on an experimental branch for six minutes, with at least 900 frames presented at up to about 5 a second. Every frame sampled was fully black, so no screen of the game has been seen. The project's own README still lists the game as not run.
projects.source: open PR #371 by a contributor, not merged; GTX 1070 Ti

projects.name: Holy-Interoperability
projects.tagline: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.furthest: One frame presented, then the game stops in its start-up code
projects.status: A retail title it does not name loads, creates its graphics device, streams its start-up data and presents its first frame after about 30 seconds, then stops in its own start-up code. The README says nothing it draws has been seen yet.

projects.name: Leonida CE
projects.tagline: Community continuation of Leonida, the first large recompilation effort
projects.furthest: The real executable submits GPU work under Wine, with stand-ins (modified)
projects.status: With exploratory stand-ins from its boot-hacks branch, the game's executable runs about a minute into start-up under Wine and submits GPU work. The README mentions a first presented frame but its own table says no frame is on screen yet, so it is placed at stage 3. A commit on 24 Nov traces a stop at 120 to 140 seconds to an incomplete pipeline map.
projects.source: project README and commit history (24 Nov); a modified build

also_watched.name: VIctory-macOS
also_watched.note: Brings VIctory to Apple Silicon Macs. It reaches only as far as VIctory does, and the world does not render yet.

also_watched.name: Leonida Continued
also_watched.note: Carries on Leonida, the first large recompilation effort, with its full history; the original repository is gone and, according to press reports, its lead stepped away. Its README says the game has never booted under this code, although all 26,503 shaders translate to SPIR-V and pass validation.

also_watched.name: Leonida (ProjectLeonidaL)
also_watched.note: Another continuation of Leonida, started on 24 Nov. Its README says the game does not boot yet; all 26,503 shaders translate to SPIR-V and pass validation.

also_watched.name: G6Recomp
also_watched.note: Static recompiler. The loader and boot milestones are in progress, and a first frame is not started.

forecast.definition: At least one project shows 30 minutes or more in the game world under player control, at 20 frames a second or better on some PC, without a crash.
rests_on: The executable surfaced on 23 November, and within about a day three code bases reported the game world running. A private build, CGBJ, is said to have done the same, but that comes from press reports only.

Other games show the pace. XCL's repository opened on the evening of 20 November, and by the evening of 22 November it listed two smaller retail games, Minecraft Preview and Unicorn Overlord, as fully playable. No project has done this with a game the size of GTA VI.

The picture is arriving. victory-gta6 renders the first gameplay scene with textures, sky and sunlit surfaces. Anything in shadow is still black, because no build runs the game's ray-traced lighting yet.

Speed is the long pole. VIctory took 0.5 to 1.8 seconds per world frame on 23 November; a day later the victory-gta6 fork runs at 2 to 4 frames a second, roughly three times faster, though on a different graphics card. Playable needs 20, so another five- to tenfold gain is still needed.

The playable bar does not require correct lighting, only 20 frames a second for 30 minutes. A build could skip the ray-traced passes to get there, as Palmwave already does with other heavy passes in its modified runs. Stability is improving: the longest reported session lasted about 13 minutes before the GPU device was lost, and on 24 Nov victory-gta6 fixed a device loss and now reports none in normal runs.
Work is shared across projects. victory-gta6, AnyXboxX and ScarlettPort build on VIctory, and fixes move between XCL, VIctory and Palmwave within days.

Takedowns are now on the record. On 24 November GitHub published a Take-Two notice against Leonida and applied it to its whole network of 3,007 repositories. The notice argues that requiring the game files, given when the project appeared and what it targets, points to the leaked copy. That argument would fit most projects listed here, though none has been named so far. A notice cannot stop private builds, but it could break up the open work the public projects depend on.

chances.label: Stalls until an official PC release

forecast.revision_note: Moved forward from Tue 1 Dec to Sun 29 Nov. The pace has been faster than this forecast assumed: frame rate roughly tripled in a day, and XCL took two smaller retail games from a new repository to playable in about two days. Reaching playable does not require ray-traced lighting, so the remaining gap is mainly speed and stability. The Take-Two notice against Leonida's 3,007-repository network is a new risk to the public projects, which is why the chance by Fri 4 Dec rises only to 7 in 10.

updates.title: Entries re-checked against every README; ScarlettPort added
points: Every entry was compared with its project's current README and recent commits. victory-gta6 now reports no device loss in normal runs after a fix, and AnyXboxX merged PR #167 and shows the 3D picture at about 4 fps.
ScarlettPort, started on 24 Nov, joins at stage 6: it reaches the movement tutorial at about 1 fps, with a black picture.

palmetto moves to stage 4: its commits report a window with presented frames and executing draws, still all black. The californiaAlmonds OpenScarlett moves to stage 5, on commits reporting the game's 4K interface and video.
Leonida CE joins at stage 3 with a modified build, and a second Leonida continuation is now watched. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: Forecast moves to Sun 29 Nov; Take-Two notice published
points: The forecast for a playable build moves from Tue 1 Dec to Sun 29 Nov. Frame rate roughly tripled in a day, XCL showed two smaller retail games going from a new repository to playable in about two days, and the playable bar does not need ray-traced lighting.
GitHub published a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida on 24 November and applied it to all 3,007 repositories in its network. No other project on this page is named in it.
No project changed stage in this check.

updates.title: Rankings rechecked; victory-gta6 takes the lead
points: Every project was rechecked against its own README, commits and pull requests. victory-gta6, a fork of VIctory, is added at the top of stage 6 with a lit first gameplay scene at 2 to 4 frames a second.
AnyXboxX's maintainer reports about 13 minutes of player-controlled play at about 4 frames a second on that fork, in an open pull request. The 30-minute, 20 fps bar for playable is not met.
g6shim moves from stage 2 to stage 5: its README shows it reaching the account picker at about 12 frames a second. The entry here was out of date.
xbox-emulator joins at stage 4 from a contributor's black-frame run. Leonida leaves the ranking because its continuation, which keeps its full history, says the game never booted under it.

updates.title: palmetto builds every pipeline; XCL moves house
points: palmetto now builds all 10,241 of the game's graphics pipelines and records about 42,700 draws per run. None executes yet, so it stays at stage 3.
XCL's repository has moved from ivall/xcl to xcl-dev/xcl. Links on this page now point to the new home.
No project changed stage in this check.

updates.title: Tracker goes live with 16 projects
points: Sixteen projects are ranked from their own READMEs, plus four on the watch list and four general Xbox layers with no GTA VI claims.
Three public projects report the game world running: AnyXboxX, VIctory and Palmwave. None has a usable picture yet.
The first forecast puts playable around Tue 1 Dec, with speed as the main obstacle.

method.label: Playable builds
method.text: None exist. Anything offered as a playable download of GTA VI for PC is fake, and fakes have carried malware.

method.label: What the projects use
method.text: They work from a leaked Xbox Series build. Rockstar has not announced a PC version. This page does not link to the leak or explain how to get or run it.

method.label: Sources
method.text: Each project's public repository: its README, status files, commits and pull requests. Press reports where a project has no public code. Every row names its source.

method.label: Claims
method.text: Stages are what each project says about itself, unless the source line says otherwise. This page does not run the code, and most claims are unverified.

method.label: Ranking
method.text: By stage first. Within a stage, by the furthest point each project has reached in the game's own sequence of screens, furthest first. When two are at about the same point, the one with a measured frame rate, an unmodified build or a public, first-hand source ranks higher. An equals sign would mark a tie that none of these separates.

method.label: Who writes it
method.text: An AI assistant (Claude) checks the repositories when asked and rewrites the entries. It can be wrong; the source links are there to check it.

method.label: Affiliation
method.text: None. Not connected to Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, Microsoft or any project listed. Names link to repositories to credit the work.
